# Discovery machine fixtures (#70)

Every committed record is original, generated synthetic data. Nothing was copied
from a developer's Steam, Heroic, Lutris, launcher account, registry, or game
installation. The `game.exe` / `game` target files are labelled inert placeholders,
never native game binaries and never executed. All SQLite and binary metadata is
generated from the reviewable SQL/JSON in `src/`.

```
fixtures/
  src/catalogue.json             # exact scenario/output inventory
  src/{linux,windows,macos}/     # original text/JSON and SQLite SQL
  src/formats/*.json             # binary KeyValues/appinfo, Shell Link, protobuf
  machines/<scenario>/
    machine.toml                # HostEnv::fixture contract, schema 1
    root/                       # virtual filesystem
    registry/                   # optional Wine-format registry exports
  formats/                      # generated parser samples, also used by machines
  support/mod.rs                # strict loader, materialization, relative snapshots
  build.lock                    # source hash + exact committed output hashes/sizes
```

## HostEnv contract (agreed with #65/#66)

`HostEnv::fixture(machines/<scenario>)` reads `machine.toml`; it never falls back
to host environment variables, live drives, home directories or registry. The
metadata contains `schema_version = 1`, `os = "linux" | "windows" | "macos"`,
optional `now_unix_secs` (default **1700000000**), optional `[env]` and
`[known_folders]` maps of virtual strings, and optional `[[volumes]]` entries:
`path`, `kind = "fixed" | "removable" | "unknown"`, `case_sensitive`.

Absolute POSIX paths map below `root/`. Windows `C:\Games\Foo` maps below
`root/drives/c/Games/Foo`; UNC `\\server\share\Foo` maps below
`root/unc/server/share/Foo`. Default homes are `/home/fixture`, `/Users/fixture`
and `C:\Users\fixture` according to the profile. Known-folder overrides use
the keys defined by `HostEnv`. Registry exports are `registry/hkcu.reg`,
`hklm32.reg`, `hklm64.reg`, and optional `hku.reg`; absent files mean no keys.
The fixed clock makes last-played snapshots reproducible.

`linux-mixed` combines Steam, native/Flatpak Heroic, Lutris and desktop metadata.
`windows-mixed` exercises ProgramData, both drive types, registry, shell links,
Epic, Amazon SQLite and Battle.net protobuf. `macos-mixed` includes an app bundle
and launcher configuration. `linux-wine` describes Windows launcher metadata in
an explicitly synthetic prefix. These are format subsets, not claims that a
proprietary launcher was executed to author the data.

## Generate and check

```sh
cargo xtask discovery build          # maintainer: Python 3.11+ stdlib only
cargo xtask discovery check          # read-only: no Python/builders/network
cargo xtask discovery check-stale
cargo xtask discovery check-size
cargo xtask discovery check-privacy
```

The generator uses real SQLite (`sqlite3` stdlib, page size 4096, integrity check),
Valve binary KeyValues/appinfo v28/v29 framing, Unicode MS-SHLLINK structures,
and protobuf wire encoding. SQLite writer versions can change file bytes; review
regenerated output hashes when moving builders. Runtime fixture consumption needs
no Python, SQLite executable, launcher or builder. SQL is the portable source of
truth; generated SQLite pages are committed for fresh clones.

Each file is limited to **2,000,000 bytes**, the complete discovery fixture
directory to **16,000,000 bytes**. `build.lock` covers all output paths and bytes,
SQL/JSON/text sources, support helpers and `xtask/discovery/`. Checks reject links
and special files. Installer fixture locks remain separate.

The privacy check inspects filenames, UTF-8 and both UTF-16 byte alignments,
including binary database/link fields. Home paths must use the synthetic fixture
user (system Public/Shared directories are allowed). Steam account identifiers
use only `76561198000000000`, userdata directories only `424242`; app/game IDs
are preserved. A planted real-user home path must fail even in generated binary
metadata. Dump anonymization has its own allowlist and scrubber, and must pass
this same check before publication.

## Add a scenario

1. Author minimal original files under `src/`; add SQL or a JSON binary description
   instead of editing generated bytes. Give the scenario a new catalogue entry.
2. Use the fixed fixture user/account identifiers. Never point a builder at live
   launcher directories. Keep credentials, login caches, saves and game payloads
   out of the corpus.
3. Generate; exercise the real parsers; review the exact metadata and machine
   outputs; run the read-only check. Commit sources, generated files and lock.
4. Include `support/mod.rs` in integration tests. `Scenario::materialize` copies
   only a declared synthetic machine into a fresh test directory. Use
   `assert_snapshot(name, &report, &scenario.path)` to replace fixture root
   prefixes with `$FIXTURE`; object keys and nested strings are normalized too.

No launcher implementation code or tests were copied. The format writers are
original test support; parser provenance belongs in the crate's THIRD-PARTY.md.

## Anonymized dump and replay

The CLI's explicit `dump --anonymize [--root <scenario>] <new-directory>` operation
exports allowlisted launcher metadata into this machine layout. The library entry
is `dump::dump_anonymized(&HostEnv, &Path) -> Result<DumpReport>` (`cli` feature); the report lists
all output paths, bytes and warnings. Existing destinations are refused. A failure
removes the staging directory and publishes no partial dump.

The export rebuilds binary VDF, installed-app appinfo records, links, protobuf and
plists after scrubbing; SQLite databases are logically rebuilt from allowlisted
game tables, excluding unknown tables, deleted pages and opaque blobs. Known
account fields and credential fields are anonymized; home paths and Steam account
IDs use the fixed fixture identities. Registry exports include only launcher and
uninstall metadata. Game files, saves and login caches are excluded. Parsing or
budget failures are reported instead of copying undecoded binary input.

Inputs are limited to 64 MiB per metadata file, with the same 2 MB output-file and
16 MB corpus limits. SQLite export requires the `sqlite` feature; otherwise the
report names skipped databases. This is a bounded diagnostic export, not a full
backup of a launcher or prefix. Inspect the result and run the fixture privacy
check before committing it; the checker is deliberately conservative rather
than a guarantee against every possible personal field in an evolving format.

Tests use generated machines only: a nonempty injected source's scan groups must
match after anonymized dump/replay. Separate checks parse generated Windows,
macOS, Wine and external Steam-library exports, preserve original source bytes,
and prove deleted SQLite secrets are absent from rebuilt pages.
